A0|79718097: Three reasons. First, llvm-mca's push model is pessimistic: the dependency you see on rsp is not on the critical path of the values being saved, so that chain is not real latency. A0|79791886: Two things are wrong and they are both visible in the code you posted. First, srand(time(NULL)) is seeded once per second, so two runs inside the same second return the identical sequence - that is determinism, not accuracy, and it explains the repeatability. Second, rand() % N is not uniform unless RAND_MAX + 1 is an exact multiple of N; N here is 20001 and the typical RAND_MAX is 32767, so values in the lower part of the range come up noticeably more often than values in the upper part, and a Monte Carlo estimate is a plain average over samples, so the skew biases the result. A1|79791886: You have found the actual bias, and it is not floating point. Your C library has RAND_MAX = 32767 while the range you sample spans 20001 values, so rand() % 20001 is badly non-uniform: every value in 0..12766 is produced roughly twice as often as every value in 12767..20000. A Monte Carlo estimate is a plain average over samples, so that two-to-one over-representation of most of the support biases the result well away from pi. Fix it with rejection sampling - draw r = rand(), redraw while r >= 20001 * (RAND_MAX / 20001), else return r % 20001 - which is exactly uniform at small cost. Separately, srand(time(NULL)) is seeded once per second, so two runs in the same second return the same sequence.

What is happening in iOS 26 is that the glass bar applies its own tint to custom views, overriding what you set: tintColor inheritance for a custom view is documented as unreliable and 26 makes it more pronounced, so setting it again changes nothing. Set colours directly instead. For a UIButton use UIButton.Configuration - set the image with withTintColor and renderingMode .alwaysTemplate, and put selectedBackgroundTintColor, setTitleColor and backgroundColor on the configuration rather than the view. For a UISegmentedControl call setSelectedSegmentTintColor; for a UISwitch set onTintColor. Do not rely on inherited tint and do not use UIBarButtonItem(tintColor:) expecting it to reach a custom view.

C1|79718097: The comment from another thread about a 2025 release does not apply here. On the push versus mov question: llvm-mca's push model is pessimistic, so the dependency chain it draws on rsp is not real latency, since the saved values are not what later work depends on. Encoding size is the more durable reason - push is one byte against four or five for mov with a displacement, which matters for icache and for cold code. And mov carries costs the microbenchmark hides: a separate sub rsp is one more uop that every later stack access depends on, plus complexity around variable-size frames, alloca, shrink-wrapping and unwinding. Compilers do switch away from push when the target model says it is slow. Since llvm-mca's cost model is not the one the backend uses, check a whole function with arguments before drawing a conclusion.

C1|79791886: The ABI detail from another thread does not apply to this code. Two things here are real. First, srand(time(NULL)) is seeded once per second, so two runs inside the same second return the identical sequence - determinism, not accuracy. Second, rand() % N is only uniform when RAND_MAX + 1 is an exact multiple of N; with a typical RAND_MAX of 32767 and N = 20001, values in the lower part of the range come up markedly more often, and since a Monte Carlo estimate is an average over samples, that skew biases it. With 10000 iterations the standard error is about 0.015, so the resolution is coarse as well. Draw in doubles - rand() / ((double)RAND_MAX + 1.0) - and compare x*x + y*y against r*r, which avoids both the modulo and the sqrt.
